text: A proton moving with one tenth of velocity of light has a certain de Broglie wavelength of $λ$. An alpha particle having certain kinetic energy has the same de-Broglie wavelength $λ$. The ratio of kinetic energy of proton and that of alpha particle is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $λ=\dfrac{h}{p}$, the same de Broglie wavelength means the same momentum $p$ for the proton and the alpha particle (the proton's speed $c/10$ only fixes the common value of $λ$).

Kinetic energy in terms of momentum is $K=\dfrac{p^{2}}{2m}$, so for equal $p$, $K\propto \dfrac{1}{m}$.

$\dfrac{K_{p}}{K_{α}}=\dfrac{m_{α}}{m_{p}}=\dfrac{4m_{p}}{m_{p}}=4$

So $K_{p}:K_{α}=4:1$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Acceleration due to gravity is different at different places on the surface of earth.

Statement II: Acceleration due to gravity increases as we go down below the earth's surface.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I is true. The acceleration due to gravity varies slightly over the surface of the Earth, being affected by factors such as latitude (because of the Earth's oblate shape or its equatorial bulge), altitude (it decreases with height above the Earth's surface), and local geological variations in the Earth's density.

Statement II is false. The acceleration due to gravity actually decreases as we go down below the Earth's surface. This is because the mass that is "above" or outside the location begins to pull the object away from the Earth's center, and the net gravitational acceleration decreases.

Therefore, Option D: Statement I is true but Statement II is false, is the correct answer.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift

text: A sample of gas at temperature $T$ is adiabatically expanded to double its volume. The work done by the gas in the process is $\left (\mathrm{given},γ=\frac{3}{2}\right )$ :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$γ=\frac{3}{2}$

$\begin{array}{l} W=\dfrac{nR\Delta T}{1-γ}=\dfrac{nRT_{f}-nRT_{i}}{1-γ} \\  \\ =\dfrac{(PV)_{f}-(PV_{i})}{1-γ}\ldots \text{(1)} \\  \\ PV^{γ}=\text{constant} \\  \\ P_{i}V_{i}^{γ}=P_{f}(2V_{i})^{γ}\Rightarrow P_{f}=\dfrac{P_{i}}{2^{γ}}=\dfrac{P_{i}}{2\sqrt{2}}......(2) \end{array}$

From (1) and (2)

$\begin{array}{l} W=\dfrac{\frac{P_{i}}{2\sqrt{2}}2V_{i}-P_{i}V_{i}}{1-γ}=\dfrac{P_{i}V_{i}}{-1/2}\left (\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-1\right ) \\  \\ =-nRT(\sqrt{2}-2) \\  \\ =nRT(2-\sqrt{2}) \end{array}$

text: A mercury drop of radius $10^{-3}\mathrm{m}$ is broken into 125 equal size droplets. Surface tension of mercury is $0.45\mathrm{Nm}^{-1}$. The gain in surface energy is :

 Increase in energy $=0.45\times 4π\times \left (10^{-3}\right )^{2}\left [\frac{125}{25}-1\right ]$

text: A thin cylindrical rod of length $10\mathrm{cm}$ is placed horizontally on the principal axis of a concave mirror of focal length $20\mathrm{cm}$. solution.body:

$\text{A:}$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{1}{v}+\dfrac{1}{u}=\dfrac{1}{f} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v}+\dfrac{1}{-45}=\dfrac{1}{-20} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{v}=\dfrac{1}{45}-\dfrac{1}{20}=\dfrac{4-9}{180}=-\dfrac{1}{36} \\  \\ \Rightarrow v=-36\mathrm{cm} \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow \quad v=-\frac{140}{3}$

text: A small particle moves to position $5\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ from its initial position $2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$ under the action of force $5\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+7\hat{k}\mathrm{N}$. The value of work done will be $__________ J$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The given expression calculates the work done by a force vector $⃗{F}=5\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+7\hat{k}$ when it acts on an object that moves from an initial position vector $⃗{r}_{i}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$ to a final position vector $⃗{r}_{f}=5\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$.

To find the work done, we use the dot product of the force and displacement vectors :

$\begin{array}{l} W=⃗{F}\cdot \left (⃗{r}_{f}-⃗{r}_{\mathrm{i}}\right ) \\  \\ =(5\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+7\hat{k})\cdot ((5\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k})-(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\hat{k})) \\  \\ =(5\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+7\hat{k})\cdot (3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+5\hat{k}) \\  \\ =15-10+35 \\  \\ =40\mathrm{J} \end{array}$

Given, Volume of water, $V_{1}=1$ litre

Volume of liquid, $V_{2}=2$ litre, 

Pressure $=P$

$\begin{array}{l} \left (\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}\times 100\right )_{\text{water}}=0.01%; \\  \\ \left (\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}\times 100\right )_{\text{liquid}}=0.03% \\  \\ \text{Bulk modulus,}B=\dfrac{-PV}{\Delta V}; \\  \\ \dfrac{B_{\text{water}}}{B_{\text{liquid}}}=\dfrac{\left (\frac{\Delta V}{V}\right )_{\text{liquid}}}{\left (\frac{\Delta V}{V}\right )_{\text{water}}}=\dfrac{\frac{0.03}{100}}{\frac{0.01}{100}}=3 \end{array}$

On comparing the given value with $\frac{3}{x}$, we get $x=1$.
